header: Date: 2025-02-20T15:00Z, Duration: 42m, Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Amy Rodriguez (CISO, First Federal), Ben Carter (Head of Platform), Raj Patel (Lead ML Engineer). Shared: security deck (link), Dedicated vs Private TCO sheet (link).
summary: Discovery focused on data residency, logging/audit constraints, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment meets First Federal Bank's regulatory needs (GDPR, HIPAA-adjacent financial controls, logging retention). Customer leans toward Dedicated or Private due to strict logging retention and regional residency requirements. Agreed to run Dedicated trial and share security artifacts.
topics: deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
00:00 Lena (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we can do quick intros then jump into your compliance needs.
00:12 Amy (CISO): Hi, Amy here. We run most services in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, financial regs require EU residency for EU customers.
00:22 Ben (Platform): Ben, head of platform, quick note we need strict control of logs and retention, cannot export raw logs off region.
00:30 Marcus (SE): Great, Marcus from Redwood. Quick note, we have Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments — each has different guarantees for residency and log access.
00:40 Raj (ML): Raj, lead ML. Our main questions: can we keep inference data and logs in-region, and how much logging does Redwood do by default?
00:50 Lena: Good. high level first: Hosted is easiest but less control — logs and metrics aggregated in Redwood-managed infra, data may transit between regions for failover, not ideal for strict residency. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in a region with optional data isolation, and Private gives you customer-managed control plane / VPC.
01:12 Amy: For us, GDPR data residency is a hard requirement for EU-origin records. Also we have internal rules around PII in logs: must mask, short retention, and audit trails for access. HIPAA isn't our primary but similar control expectations.
01:28 Marcus: Understood. On Dedicated we can pin capacity to eu-west-1 and ensure logs are stored in that region; we offer KMS integrations so keys can be customer-owned which prevents Redwood from decrypting artifact at rest.
01:40 Ben: So KMS integration means we can manage keys in our AWS KMS? Any HSM support?
01:45 Marcus: Yes, we support customer KMS; HSM-backed keys via AWS CloudHSM or external HSMs for Private deployments. For Hosted there are more limited KMS controls.
01:58 Raj: How about request/response logging — the tokens or raw prompts — are those persisted? We need guarantee that prompts with PII aren't retained or are scrubbed.
02:08 Lena: Good question. We have policies: default logging captures high-level telemetry; payload logging (full transcripts) is optional and off by default for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted some customers opt-in; for enterprise we can disable request body retention entirely and only keep aggregated metrics.
02:27 Amy: Are there audit logs for who accessed keys / models / logs? We need evidence for audits.
02:33 Marcus: Yes, RBAC + audit logs are available. For Dedicated and Private we can push logs to your S3 or SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) in region, and they contain role-based access events.
02:48 Ben: How detailed are the audit logs? Do they include prompt contents or just metadata?
02:53 Marcus: By default metadata: request IDs, timestamps, model version, user ID, token counts. Prompt contents are separate and only retained if you enable request capture — we recommend masking PII at the client side before sending, or using our parameterized redaction tooling.
03:10 Raj: Masking at client side is doable but we need some use cases that need raw prompts for troubleshooting or evals. Is there a secure one-off export process?
03:18 Marcus: Yes — we have secure export workflows with time-limited access and can require customer KMS unwrap for retrieval; it's audited and goes through access approvals. For Private you can keep logs fully on-prem.
03:32 Amy: For GDPR, we also care about cross-border transfers for backups and failover. If we pin to eu-west-1 but failover goes to us-east-1, that's problematic.
03:41 Lena: Right — we can configure routing policies to avoid cross-border failover for Dedicated/Private. Hosted may have broader failover. We can set SLOs and region-based routing to prefer capacity in-region, plus automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in-region.
03:58 Ben: Can you describe how encryption-in-transit and at-rest are handled? We need TLS plus customer-managed KMS for at-rest.
04:06 Marcus: TLS for all in-transit. For at-rest, we support customer-managed keys for model artifacts, logs, and snapshots. On Dedicated, you can elect to have persistent caches and KV stores encrypted with your KMS key.
04:21 Raj: You mentioned KV cache — is the KV cache shared across tenants or isolated? We're concerned about leakage.
04:28 Marcus: KV cache is isolated per deployment/tenant. In Dedicated each tenant's cache runs on dedicated GPU nodes; Private is fully customer-controlled.
04:36 Amy: About certifications — can you provide SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, pen test reports? Also any finance-specific controls?
04:46 Lena: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO summaries. For financial controls we map to common frameworks (we can provide control matrices). We'll include those in the security pack.
04:56 Ben: Any previous bank customers references?
05:00 Lena: We have a couple of regional banks using Dedicated with VPC peering and customer KMS; can share anonymized references.
05:09 Raj: Performance question — latencies when running in eu-west-1 Dedicated vs Hosted? We need <150ms tail for chat use case.
05:18 Marcus: It depends on model and sequence length; for small chat models in Dedicated on A100-equivalent we see p50 ~40ms, p95 ~140ms with our batching and KV cache. We'll run benchmarks with your typical payloads.
05:34 Ben: Cost vs Dedicated vs Private? High level — Dedicated predictability vs Hosted lower ops but maybe higher unit cost.
05:41 Lena: Exactly. Hosted is lower initial ops overhead but less control; Dedicated has predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale; Private has highest control and ops burden. We'll share a TCO sheet.
05:55 Amy: Logging retention specifics — we have to keep audit trails for seven years for certain transactions; but prompts with PII must be deleted in 30 days. Can Redwood support retention policies per event type?
06:08 Marcus: Yes, retention policies are configurable. For Dedicated/Private we can configure separate buckets and lifecycle rules. We can also set automated PII redaction before write.
06:20 Raj: Are you able to do on-prem deployment if regulators require no cloud?
06:24 Marcus: Yes, Private deployment offers on-prem packaged option, customer-managed control plane, and we support air-gapped installs. Those require extra integration work and a Professional Services engagement.
06:35 Ben: Network wise, do you support VPC peering or PrivateLink? We prefer PrivateLink for security.
06:41 Marcus: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and dedicated transit options depending on cloud provider. For Private on-prem we do VPN or direct connect equivalents.
06:52 Amy: For incident response we need access to logs and the ability to revoke keys quickly; how fast can keys be rotated and revoked?
06:59 Marcus: If you're using customer KMS, you control key rotation and revocation; we can also operate with short-lived service credentials and have emergency lockout options.
07:10 Raj: How are model updates and rollouts handled? We need canarying and ability to pin a model revision for production for compliance.
07:18 Lena: We support pinning model versions and rollout policies — canary, A/B, automatic fallback. For Dedicated/Private you control the rollout window.
07:26 Ben: If we need to do redaction of PII at the edge, does Redwood provide SDKs?
07:30 Marcus: Yes, SDKs and prebuilt client-side redaction helpers. We also provide eval tooling to compare pre/post redaction quality.
07:40 Amy: About legal — will Redwood sign data processing agreements and take on standard GDPR clauses?
07:44 Lena: Yes, we have standard DPA templates and can negotiate specific clauses for enterprise. For Private deployments we offer options to limit Redwood access.
07:52 Raj: One more: Do you keep embeddings or derived artifacts? Our policy treats embeddings as sensitive if derived from PII.
07:59 Marcus: Embeddings and derived artifacts can be configured the same as logs — disabled persist by default, or stored in-region with customer-managed KMS. We also provide auto-expiry and scrub tooling.
08:12 Ben: Any limits on retention for backups or multi-region replication? We need control over backups and ensure backups don't cross borders.
08:21 Marcus: On Dedicated and Private, backups can be scoped to region and retention controlled via lifecycle policies. For Hosted we'd need to discuss special contractual restrictions.
08:31 Amy: Good. For our internal eval, timeline is two phases: security/compliance sign-off and then a pilot with real traffic. Target is pilot in Q2.
08:40 Lena: Sounds good — pilot in Q2 is feasible. We'll provide the security pack and TCO, and run benchamrks.
08:47 Raj: For the benchmarks — we'll give sample payloads and expected QPS.
08:51 Marcus: Perfect. We'll schedule the benchmark session; we'll also provision a short Dedicated trial so you can run it in your own VPC if desired.
09:00 Ben: One concern: we sometimes need to redact user identifiers from logs but keep traceability. Is there a recommended pattern?
09:06 Marcus: Use deterministic hashing with salted keys managed by your KMS — keeps traceability but not raw PII. We can share patterns.
09:15 Amy: Okay, let's recap next steps.
09:18 Lena: Recap: we'll send security pack (SOC2/ISO, pen test summary), Dedicated vs Private TCO, and schedule the benchmark and tech deep dive. You (Raj) will share sample payloads and QPS.
09:30 Ben: Agreed. Also we'd like to see an anonymized reference for another bank.
09:34 Lena: We'll include that.
09:36 Amy: Thanks everyone.
09:38 Lena: Thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and calendar invite for tech deep dive.
09:42 [call ends]

Note: transcript contains typical ASR artifacts and occasional speaker overlap; names in parentheticals are inferred. Some technical terms: KV cache, KMS, HSM, VPC, PrivateLink, SOC2 mentioned. Some words may be slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., "canary" spoken fast).
